title: Subdomain Visit Count
statement:
Each entry of `cpdomains` is a visit count, one space, and then a domain made of two or three dot-separated labels, such as `"9001 discuss.leetcode.com"`. Each visit to a domain is also a visit to every shorter domain obtained by dropping labels from its left end: visits to `discuss.leetcode.com` also count for `leetcode.com` and for `com`.

Add up the visits each domain receives this way across all entries, and return one string per distinct domain in the form `"<total> <domain>"`. The strings may be returned in any order.
constraints: rep is an integer from 1 to 10^4
d1, d2 and d3 contain only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Every entry contributes its visit count to a handful of domains: the full domain and each suffix that starts right after a dot. So the task is pure counting: one running total per domain name, keyed in a hash map. A slower way would gather every suffix of every entry into a list and search that list for each name, but a map makes each update constant time.

## Approach

1. Create an empty map `counts` from domain name to total visits.
2. For each `entry`, find the `space`, read `visits` from the text before it and `domain` from the text after it.
3. Add `visits` to the full `domain`.
4. Scan `domain`; at every dot, the text after it is a `parent` domain, so add `visits` to that too.
5. Turn each map entry into the string `total + ' ' + domain` and return the list.

## Example 1, step by step

The single entry `"9001 discuss.leetcode.com"` has `space` at index 4, so `visits = 9001` and `domain = "discuss.leetcode.com"`. That domain gets 9001. The dot at index 7 gives `parent = "leetcode.com"`, and the dot at index 16 gives `parent = "com"`; each gets 9001. The result is `["9001 discuss.leetcode.com", "9001 leetcode.com", "9001 com"]`, which matches in any order.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · L), where n is the number of entries and L their length: each entry is scanned once and makes at most three map updates.
- Space: O(n · L) for the map keys, since each entry adds at most three distinct names.

## Pitfalls

- Convert the visit count to a number before adding; adding the raw text concatenates strings.
- The same domain can appear in several entries (or as a parent of several), so always add to the existing total instead of overwriting it.
- Only split at dots after the space; the visit count itself never becomes a domain.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `counts` | map from domain name to its total visits |
| `entry` | the current count-paired domain string |
| `space` | index of the space between the count and the domain |
| `visits` | the entry's visit count as a number |
| `domain` | the entry's full domain |
| `parent` | a shorter domain that follows a dot in `domain` |
| `result` | the output strings |

narration.2: A map holds the running total of visits for every domain name seen so far.
narration.3: Process the count-paired entries one at a time.
narration.4: Find the space that separates the count from the domain.
narration.5: The text before the space is the visit count; convert it to a number.
narration.6: The text after the space is the full domain.
narration.7: The full domain itself receives all of this entry's visits.
narration.8: Walk through the domain's characters looking for dots.
narration.9: Every dot marks the start of a parent domain.
narration.10: The parent domain is everything after this dot.
narration.11: The parent is visited implicitly, so it receives the same visits.
narration.15: Build the output list from the finished totals.
narration.16: Go through every domain with its total visits.
narration.17: Each pair becomes one "total domain" string.
narration.19: Return the strings; any order is accepted.
